nodes.label: CI/CD invariants (what not to break)
nodes.rationale: Vulnerability gates fail closed with only a dated exception as escape hatch; NuGet lock files + --locked-mode must be regenerated with any bump; third-party Actions pinned to full commit SHA (post trivy-action/tj-actions compromises); CI publishes per-commit images that the release PR only ever promotes (retags), never rebuilds, so a version tag always points at already-gated bytes.

nodes.label: Two commit-message traps that silently cost a release entry
nodes.norm_label: two commit-message traps that silently cost a release entry
nodes.rationale: A squashed PR's release note comes from the PR title, which no local hook can see; and a body line matching word(...(...)  breaks the conventional-commit parser, silently dropping the whole commit from the changelog while the release workflow still reports success. Both traps produce a green run with no release entry, motivating the local commit-msg hook that catches the second case.

nodes.label: Collectify design system overview
nodes.rationale: Collectify should feel like a private, well-kept media shelf: calm enough for daily cataloging, bright enough to make collecting feel satisfying, leaning into a self-hosted/private/open-source promise via clear status surfaces and direct language rather than marketing copy.

nodes.label: Opt-in Git Hooks (.githooks)
nodes.rationale: A hook nobody can bypass gets bypassed anyway (via core.hooksPath), so hooks are opt-in and explicitly skippable. Making the escape hatch obvious keeps the hook installed. CI remains the authority for correctness; hooks only shorten the loop.

nodes.label: SKIP_HOOKS / --no-verify escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Skipping is allowed on purpose: an unbypassable hook just gets disabled entirely via core.hooksPath, so a visible, sanctioned skip keeps the hook installed and catching things most of the time.

nodes.label: Publish-by-commit then promote-by-retag pattern
nodes.rationale: Every merge publishes :sha-<commit>, scanned and boot-tested; the release workflow later promotes one of those exact digests to :vX.Y.Z via a server-side retag, never a rebuild — so a versioned tag is guaranteed to point at bytes CI already gated, and a rebuild would silently break that guarantee by producing unscanned bytes.

nodes.label: Releases & container images (two-stage publish/promote)
nodes.rationale: CI publishes an image per merge (Trivy-scanned, boot-tested, attested); merging the release-please PR promotes that exact commit's already-scanned digest to :vX.Y.Z via a server-side retag rather than a rebuild, so the version tag always points at bytes CI already gated, and a failed promotion leaves no tag pointing at nothing. Deploy by digest, never by tag, and verify via gh attestation verify.

nodes.rationale: Every query against a collection table must filter by OwnerId even though the app ships single-user, so cross-owner leaks reduce to a greppable pattern instead of a latent multi-user bug.

nodes.label: Central Package Management (Directory.Packages.props)
nodes.rationale: All NuGet versions live centrally with ManagePackageVersionsCentrally on so version drift and floating transitive versions can't sneak in per-project; PackageReference entries must omit Version or the build fails.

nodes.label: Conventional commits feed the changelog
nodes.rationale: PR titles become release notes via release-please; a non-conventional or typo'd prefix silently costs a changelog line and a version bump.

nodes.label: DLC/add-on schema hook (Game.ParentGameId self-FK)
nodes.rationale: Steam, Xbox and PSN all model DLC as a separate product linked to a base game, so one self-reference (ParentGameId) covers every storefront without per-provider schema branching; imports stay flat with no auto-linking in this iteration.

nodes.label: Clean/Onion Architecture layering
nodes.rationale: Small, maintainable Clean/Onion-style architecture keeps domain logic free of framework concerns; the dependency arrow points inward only (Api -> Infrastructure -> Domain), making it straightforward to add Phase 2 metadata providers and Phase 3 barcode lookup without leaking framework types into Domain.

nodes.label: Migration policy (never edit an applied migration)
nodes.norm_label: migration policy (never edit an applied migration)
nodes.rationale: Migrations are write-once-deploy-everywhere; editing one already applied to someone's database corrupts their schema history, so a new migration is required instead.

nodes.label: What we are NOT doing (no CQRS/MediatR/AutoMapper/premature interfaces)
nodes.norm_label: what we are not doing (no cqrs/mediatr/automapper/premature interfaces)
nodes.rationale: The codebase is too small to justify CQRS/MediatR/AutoMapper indirection or repository/service interfaces introduced purely for swappability; only abstract things genuinely substituted (external providers, time). Revisit only if growth past Phase 3 makes the constraint hurt.

nodes.label: C1 fix: composite FK (GameId,OwnerId) + Restrict + explicit null-out on delete
nodes.norm_label: c1 fix: composite fk (gameid,ownerid) + restrict + explicit null-out on delete
nodes.rationale: A composite FK with nullable GameId but required OwnerId breaks DELETE /api/games/{id}: SetNull would null every child column including the required OwnerId, and NoAction would fail the delete outright. Fix: add alternate key (Id,OwnerId) on Games, DeleteBehavior.Restrict on the ledger FK, and change GamesEndpoints DELETE to null only GameStoreOwnedTitle.GameId in an owner-scoped transaction before deleting the Game.

nodes.label: Provider seam decision: Steam-concrete, no Domain-level interface
nodes.norm_label: provider seam decision: steam-concrete, no domain-level interface
nodes.rationale: The v2 plan's generic IPlatformGameImportProvider in Domain was the worst of both worlds: five hardcoded /api/accounts/steam/* routes already existed and OpenID auth isn't behind the seam anyway (Xbox/PSN need entirely different auth). Resolution matches architecture.md:141-148 ('no service interfaces purely for swappability... don't pre-introduce') -- shared logic lives in one Infrastructure SteamStoreImportService; Xbox/PS get their own endpoint groups later.

nodes.label: Second-factor browser-bound cookie (S1)
nodes.rationale: The server stores only the hash of an opaque random state and additionally sets a short-lived HttpOnly SameSite=Lax Secure cookie holding a random second half, so a leaked state URL alone (e.g. via reverse-proxy logs) can't complete a Steam account link.

nodes.label: Corrupt exceptions file silent-warn bug
nodes.rationale: A corrupt exceptions file suppressed nothing but also warned nothing; loadExceptions now warns on unparseable JSON, a non-array exceptions key, or an unreadable file, while a missing file (the normal case) stays quiet.

nodes.label: Where each CI security gate runs (blocking vs advisory)
nodes.norm_label: where each ci security gate runs (blocking vs advisory)

nodes.label: Unknown --level threshold fail-open bug
nodes.rationale: severityRank() correctly ranks an unknown finding severity above critical, but the same ranking applied to the threshold puts the floor out of reach for a typo like '--level hihg', so a real critical reports below threshold and the gate exits 0; isKnownLevel now gates it in both main() and gate().

nodes.label: Draft release until promotion succeeds
nodes.rationale: GitHub withholds the git tag for a draft release, so a run that cannot find a verified image leaves no tag and no public release rather than a version pointing at nothing; safe because manifest mode reads the version from .release-please-manifest.json, not tags.

nodes.label: /api/health version stamped at build time from version.txt
nodes.norm_label: /api/health version stamped at build time from version.txt
nodes.rationale: Promotion never rebuilds, so the version can't be stamped at release time; instead CI passes VERSION=<version.txt> and INFORMATIONAL_VERSION=<version.txt>+<short-sha> at build time, so a released image reports the real version and an interim commit image reports <last release>+<sha>.

nodes.label: Multi-arch build (amd64 scanned+booted, arm64 scanned only)
nodes.norm_label: multi-arch build (amd64 scanned+booted, arm64 scanned only)
nodes.rationale: amd64 is built natively, Trivy-scanned, and boot-tested; arm64 is built from the same source/cache and independently Trivy-scanned but not boot-tested (emulated .NET+Postgres boot is too slow/flaky to gate on), trading the old single-arch byte-level scanned==published proof for arch coverage.

nodes.label: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures mitigations
nodes.norm_label: a08: software and data integrity failures mitigations

nodes.label: Decision records index
nodes.rationale: Each decision record holds the relocated narrative rationale for a rule that appears compressed in AGENTS.md or README.md, reachable via a -> link, so the resident summary stays short while the earned reasoning stays discoverable.

nodes.label: Turn OFF CodeQL default setup (one-time repo setting)
nodes.norm_label: turn off codeql default setup (one-time repo setting)
nodes.rationale: codeql.yml is an advanced configuration; GitHub refuses to ingest its SARIF while default setup is enabled, so Analyze jobs stay red until an owner manually switches Code scanning to advanced in repo settings.

nodes.label: Digest pinning + full-commit-SHA action pinning
nodes.rationale: Dockerfile base images pin to immutable @sha256 digests and third-party GitHub Actions pin to a full commit SHA (never a mutable tag) because a tag can be re-pointed to malicious code, as happened to aquasecurity/trivy-action (2026-03) and tj-actions/changed-files (2025-03).

nodes.label: Fail-closed gate design
nodes.rationale: Unreadable input, an unrecognised report shape, an unknown severity, or a malformed exception all err toward blocking; motivated by npm audit printing {error:...} with non-zero exit on a registry failure, which a naive '|| true' would otherwise treat as clean (fail open).

nodes.label: System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.7 -> 10.0.11 bump
nodes.rationale: 10.0.7 was pinned specifically to fix two older advisories but collected five of its own; bumping the whole 10.0.x family to 10.0.11 cleared all six high-severity advisories (including the transitive SQLitePCLRaw one) -- the lesson: keep the pin ahead of advisories, treat a gate failure as 'bump this' not 'except it'.

nodes.label: vuln-gate.mjs security gate script
nodes.rationale: npm audit --audit-level=high has no allowlist (one unfixable advisory blocks every PR) and dotnet list package --vulnerable always exits 0, so a custom script parses both into one exceptions file, one severity ladder, and one report format.

nodes.label: GitHub App token for release-please instead of repo-wide PR-write setting
nodes.norm_label: github app token for release-please instead of repo-wide pr-write setting
nodes.rationale: Flipping the repo-wide 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' setting frees the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN for every job with pull-requests:write; a scoped GitHub App keeps that gate off and additionally lets the release PR trigger CI, which a GITHUB_TOKEN-opened PR cannot. The private key is a repo secret, so safety comes from no PR-controlled job referencing it, not from permission-* downscoping alone.

nodes.label: published-digest-<sha> artifact lookup by name
nodes.rationale: A registry tag like :sha-<commit> is mutable and could be forged in the window before CI finishes; promotion instead reads a build-bound artifact by name (not by run) because a repair dispatch reports the branch tip as head_sha, which a run-keyed lookup would miss. The artifact's mere existence proves build-and-test, client, entrypoint and image all passed.

nodes.label: Digest promotion (server-side retag, never rebuild)
nodes.rationale: The old release.yml rebuilt the image from a v* tag, producing different bytes (fresh timestamps, layer metadata) than the digest CI had scanned. Promotion is now a server-side retag (docker buildx imagetools create --prefer-index=false) so the version tag resolves to exactly the bytes Trivy-scanned and boot-tested; --prefer-index=false matters because the true default wraps the manifest in a new index with a different digest.

nodes.label: Build-provenance attestation verification (gh attestation verify)
nodes.rationale: promote verifies --bundle-from-oci (referrer stored beside the image), --signer-workflow (binds identity to the ci.yml path, not just the repo) and --source-ref (binds to main, since workflow_dispatch runs whichever ref's ci.yml is chosen). Together these close a leaked registry credential and a branch-push substitution, but not a change merged to main itself -- that needs PR review, which main does not yet require.

nodes.label: C3: Postgres EnsureCreatedAsync no-op on existing DB
nodes.community_name: Phase 5 photo-snap visual lookup design spec
nodes.norm_label: c3: postgres ensurecreatedasync no-op on existing db
nodes.rationale: SQLite runs MigrateAsync() but Postgres runs EnsureCreatedAsync() (Program.cs:88-98), which is a no-op against an existing database, so on an existing Postgres install the new Steam-import tables are NOT created and the endpoints would 500. This is a pre-existing repo limitation now surfaced by the first feature to add tables since it was introduced; rollout must require a Postgres volume reset and must not promise 'no behavior change'.

nodes.label: TDD workflow (Red -> Green -> Refactor)
nodes.community_name: Phase 5 photo-snap visual lookup design spec
nodes.rationale: The data model is still evolving across phases, so tests are the contract that survives refactors; multi-user readiness depends on every query filtering by OwnerId, and a regression there is a security bug, not a feature bug -- tests are the only defense.
